name: Zero scalar rule
summary: The zero scalar absorbs any other scalar spider.
description:
A Z-spider with phase π and no legs is the scalar 0, so it absorbs any other scalar, in particular a Z-spider with no legs and any phase α (which is the scalar $1+e^{i\alpha}$).

Backens added this rule, together with the [zero rule](../zero-rule/), to make the stabilizer ZX-calculus with scalars complete for zero diagrams (there α is a multiple of π/2). Backens, Perdrix and Wang later showed that it is derivable from the other rules.

source.location: Section 4.3 (Completeness for stabilizer zero diagrams), zero scalar rule

also_in.location: Figure 1, rule (ZS); Section 3.2 shows it is not necessary
